display.purpose: The one big number on the desk figure sheet; odometer digits. Anek at width 75%.

headline.purpose: Today's single action on the slip; farmer name and picking date are siblings.

title.purpose: Sheet-head titles, paired with a Marathi title in Tiro.

body.purpose: Captions, ledger rows, explanations; 14–15px on the phone; locks to the rule pitch on ruled paper.

label.purpose: Uppercase printed labels on forms and column heads only; never a kicker above a heading.

typed.purpose: Courier Prime: every computed record value, date, time, ID, price and form code.

ballpoint.purpose: Kalam in Ballpoint Blue: entries a person made, voice transcripts.

marathi-title.purpose: Tiro Devanagari Marathi beside English titles and on the today slip's Marathi action.

marathi-body.purpose: Anek Devanagari partner line for every farmer-facing line; map and tab subtitles.

shadows.name: shadow-sheet
shadows.purpose: A sheet lying on the manila board; a stamp button while pressed.

shadows.name: shadow-lift
shadows.purpose: Held above the paper: hover cards, floating slips, stamp buttons at rest.

shadows.name: tab-lip
shadows.purpose: Top edge of the active file tab.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.value: spring(stiffness 700, damping 26, mass 0.6); from scale 1.3, opacity 0.45, rotate −4° extra; to scale 1, opacity 0.92
motion.purpose: Every rubber stamp and dated impression pressing onto the sheet.

motion.name: stamp-button-press
motion.purpose: Pressing a StampButton into the board.

motion.name: ink-spread
motion.purpose: Flash of ink on each StampButton pointer-down.

motion.name: odometer
motion.purpose: Date-stamp digits and poster figures roll rather than swap.

motion.name: month-roll
motion.purpose: The date stamp's month band rolling up or down.

motion.name: re-ink
motion.purpose: Marks and values re-inking when the day changes; future marks turning to pencil.

motion.name: map-fill
motion.purpose: Village areas re-shading on the survey map.

motion.name: paper-slide
motion.purpose: Full-height phone sheets (Scan a leaf, Ask) sliding up like paper.

motion.name: slip-slide
motion.purpose: Today slip and ripple slip arriving.

motion.name: tab-paper
motion.purpose: The active file tab's paper moving between tabs.

motion.name: listening-rings
motion.purpose: Microphone orb while listening (skipped under reduced motion).

motion.name: season-clock
motion.value: 0.65 simulated days per second; 0.035 during the 05:00–07:00 run on the Runs layer
motion.purpose: Vehicles and hours move only through simulated time.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; stamp presses, ink spreads and blur are skipped.

narrative.overview:
KhetKundli is drawn as the paperwork of a Maharashtra plot: the 7/12 extract, the Soil Health Card, the village survey map. Every surface is a stack of cool ruled register sheets lying on a manila file board. Modules are entries in a record and the collective layers are the survey map, so the interface vocabulary is the vocabulary of a government file: numbered form fields, typed values, ballpoint notes, rubber stamps, perforated carbon slips, file tabs and a dated stamp.

Provenance is carried by ink, not by badges. Carbon-black typewriter marks anything computed, ballpoint blue in a human hand marks anything a person entered, and violet rubber stamps mark verified state and "now". Red ink appears only when something needs attention. One axis, the season's day, drives everything: rolling the date stamp on the desk or turning the kundli wheel on the phone re-inks every sheet, the map and the runs together.

The two built surfaces share the world but not the density. The Taluka Desk is a dense, projector-scale operations board; the farmer phone is a single column of large, bilingual, high-contrast sheets for one-handed outdoor use. The world refuses the agritech default of KPI tiles over a satellite basemap with coloured pins, and the farmer-app default of a feed of tips, weather tiles and a chatbot bubble.
keyCharacteristics: Manila board ground, cool register paper, warm brown shadows.
Three provenance inks (typed carbon, Kalam ballpoint, violet stamp) plus red ink for alerts only.
Anek Latin and Anek Devanagari on the width axis for all UI; Courier Prime only for record values; Tiro Devanagari Marathi for Marathi titles.
Survey-map linework with H3 hexes hatched in red ink for blight risk; no individual farm on a shared view.
Motion is physical and driven by simulated time: stamps press, digits roll, ink re-fades, paper slides.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Every value is written in exactly one ink, and the ink says who wrote it: typed carbon for computed, Kalam ballpoint blue for a person, violet stamp for verified or current state. A value never carries two inks and is never coloured for decoration.

rules.name: The Red Ink Rule
rules.body: Red means attention: risk, failure, glut, low confidence, offline, re-planned. When an entry is an alert, red replaces its ink colour but its typeface keeps its provenance. The one ledger-native exception is a deduction on a sale slip, written in red as a debit.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper is cool grey-green register stock, never cream. Warmth belongs to the manila board around it.

rules.name: The Typewriter Is for Values Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime sets only record values, codes, dates, times and numbers. Labels, headings and prose are Anek. If it was computed, it is typed.

rules.name: The Marathi Alongside Rule
rules.body: Every farmer-facing line carries its Marathi partner in the same block, at equal or near-equal size, never behind a toggle. Titles pair with Tiro Devanagari Marathi; body lines with Anek Devanagari.

rules.name: The Form Code Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading. A sheet is identified by a typed form code (KK-1 to KK-7, or the plot ID) in the right cluster of its head, beside its stamps. No kicker, no eyebrow.

rules.name: The Ruled Pitch Rule
rules.body: On ruled paper, line-height equals the rule gap and the date or time column sits in the margin. Text never floats between rules.

rules.name: The Paper on Board Rule
rules.body: A thing either lies on the board (sheet), is held above it (lift), or is pressed into it: a stamp button drops 2px and collapses from lift to sheet. Nothing inside a sheet casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Stamp Every Source Rule
rules.body: Every block of data carries a LIVE or SIMULATED stamp in its head or beside its figure. A source that is not live is never presented as live; the pomegranate scan result stays SIMULATED until a pomegranate model exists.

rules.name: The Simulated Clock Rule
rules.body: Nothing moves on its own. Vehicles, hours and marks move only when simulated time moves (play, roll, drag). Under reduced motion every animation and transition collapses to 1ms, and stamp presses, ink spreads, month blur and listening rings are skipped.

dos: Do write every value in the ink of whoever produced it: typed carbon (Courier Prime) for computed, Kalam ballpoint blue for a person, a violet stamp for verified or current state.
Do stamp every data source LIVE (violet) or SIMULATED (carbon), on the sheet head or beside the figure it qualifies.
Do set Marathi alongside every farmer-facing line: Tiro Devanagari Marathi for titles, Anek Devanagari for body lines.
Do give every phone control at least 48px in its smaller dimension, and the dock's primary stamp buttons 64px.
Do identify a sheet by its typed form code (KK-1 to KK-7, or the plot ID) at the right end of its head.
Do re-ink with a 200ms fade when the day changes, press stamps on the spring, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do put tear-off notices (today's action, re-planned ripples, demo inputs, escalations, scan advice) on the perforated yellow slip.
Do aggregate shared maps to H3 hexes and village areas, drawing risk as red-ink hatching density.
donts: Don't place a kicker or eyebrow above any heading; the form code and stamps in the head's right cluster are the only marks a sheet head carries.
Don't use red for anything but alerts and ledger debits: never for decoration, brand or "today".
Don't put two inks on one value, or colour a value outside its provenance ink or the alert.
Don't add coloured side-stripe borders to cards, rows or alerts; the register's red margin rule is ruling printed on the paper, not a status stripe.
Don't use progress rings or radial gauges for a metric; the kundli wheel is a season chart (time round the circle), not a percentage.
Don't use cream or warm paper; warmth belongs to the manila board.
Don't build KPI tiles over a satellite basemap with coloured pins, or a feed of tips, weather tiles and a chatbot bubble.
Don't show an individual farm on a shared map.
Don't animate vehicles or the season unless simulated time is moving.
